clue.text: Illusive appearance to accept with plug in

indicators.note: 'with ... in' says one part is put inside the other

parts.note: to face something is to accept it
a plug is an advertisement, shortened to AD

explanation.surface: An instruction for making an appearance: take something on board, with an electric plug fitted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plug' suggests the electrical sort, but here it is the promotional kind, a puff for a product.
explanation.definitionFit: A facade is a deceptive outward show, a false front hiding the reality behind it.

clue.text: Does Joan vouch for regular feeling of having been here before?

definitions.text: feeling of having been here before

indicators.note: regular means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the first, third, fifth letters and so on of these words

explanation.surface: Asking whether Joan will vouch for a familiar, recurring sensation.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking alternate letters from the D gives DEJAVU; the final H of vouch is left over.
explanation.definitionFit: Déjà vu, French for 'already seen', is the uncanny sense that a new experience has happened before.

clue.text: Flower container hit, causing commotion

parts.note: a flower bed holds flowers
to lam is to beat or hit hard

explanation.surface: Someone knocks over a flowerpot and causes an uproar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower container' suggests a vase or pot, but the gardening sense, a bed, is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedlam, from the old London asylum of Bethlem, means a scene of noisy uproar and confusion.

clue.text: Penchant for Long Island leader

parts.note: the standard abbreviation for Long Island, New York
a king is a leader of a country

explanation.surface: Someone has a soft spot for the man who runs Long Island.
explanation.definitionFit: A penchant is a fondness or taste for something, which is exactly what a liking is.

clue.text: Ice tea far out in staff restaurant

indicators.note: letters that are out of place are put back in a different order

parts.note: the nine letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Iced tea is a long way off in the works canteen.
explanation.definitionFit: A cafeteria is a self-service eating place, typically one provided for employees at work.

clue.text: Banker's car in fine shape

indicators.note: putting letters into a new shape rearranges them; 'fine' is also among them

parts.note: the nine letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A banker's motor is in excellent condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banker's' reads as possessive, but it is 'Banker is'. The words 'in' and 'fine' belong to the fodder as well as the surface phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A financier is someone who manages large sums of money, as a banker does.

clue.text: Craftily eat it after All Saints' Day for trial period

parts.note: All Saints' Day falls on 1 November, written NOV and I for one

indicators.note: doing something craftily means doing it with cunning twists, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A sly suggestion to tuck in once the feast of All Saints is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places the rearranged letters after the date.
explanation.definitionFit: A novitiate is the probationary period a novice spends before taking religious vows.

clue.text: Noisy little insect about to trap one bounder

indicators.note: something that traps holds the other parts inside it

parts.note: CA is short for circa, meaning about
the Roman numeral for one
a bounder is a cad, a dishonourable man

explanation.surface: A noisy bug is about to catch a single jumping creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bounder' suggests something that leaps, but it is old British slang for a cad.
explanation.definitionFit: The cicada is a small insect famous for the loud, shrill buzzing the males make.

clue.text: Why a clock's useless — return what's supplied

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so the phrase is read from end to start

parts.note: a clock with no face to read cannot tell you the time

explanation.surface: A broken clock is sent back to the shop that provided it.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening is a riddle: the clock is useless because it has NO DIAL; read backwards that gives LAID ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Something laid on has been provided or arranged, as with transport or food supplied for guests.

clue.text: Six find a way

parts.note: the Roman numeral for six
taken as written

explanation.surface: Half a dozen people manage to work out a route.
explanation.definitionFit: Via is Latin for road, and in English names the route taken, as in travelling via Paris.

clue.text: Possibly get a gold finish on cake

indicators.note: a finish on something comes at its end, so this piece is placed last
possibly signals one of several ways the letters could be arranged

parts.note: letters to be rearranged
AU is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A baker might give a cake a gilded finishing touch.
explanation.definitionFit: Gateau, from the French for cake, is a rich layered cake, usually with cream.

clue.text: Grass bristle in middle of lawns

indicators.note: the middle of a word is its inside, so the letters lie within it

parts.note: the word minus its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A spiky blade of grass stands out in the middle of a lawn.
explanation.definitionFit: An awn is the stiff, hair-like bristle growing from the seed head of grasses such as barley.

clue.text: Mother has good food for bird

parts.note: an informal word for mother
G is the abbreviation for good; 'has' attaches it
a pie is a kind of food

explanation.surface: Mum has something tasty prepared to feed the birds.
explanation.definitionFit: The magpie is a black-and-white member of the crow family, known for collecting shiny objects.

clue.text: Commander once more not at home

indicators.note: not means without, so the following letters are taken away

parts.note: once more means again
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: A former commander is out of the house yet again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Commander once' looks like the definition, but 'once' belongs with 'more'. An aga was a military commander in the Ottoman Empire.
explanation.definitionFit: Aga is a title for a military officer or chief in the Ottoman Empire, a commander by rank.

clue.text: Yearning for a prominent feature — good!

parts.note: A, plus a chin, a feature that can stick out of a face
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Someone longs for a striking facial feature and cheers at getting one.
explanation.definitionFit: Aching can mean longing intensely, as in aching to see someone again.

clue.text: Ahead of boy, new unopened office container

indicators.note: with its opening gone, a word loses its first letter
ahead of means in front of, so the following piece comes before the boy

parts.note: mint means brand new, as in mint condition
Ray is a boy's name

explanation.surface: Before the lad arrives, a brand-new office box sits still sealed.
explanation.definitionFit: An in-tray is a desk tray holding incoming documents still to be dealt with.

clue.text: Listened to guy spring at intervals

indicators.note: what is listened to is heard, so the spoken word counts rather than its spelling

parts.note: geezer is British slang for a man or guy

explanation.surface: Someone paid attention to a man who leaps up every so often.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech GEYSER is said 'geezer', the slang word for a bloke.
explanation.definitionFit: A geyser is a hot spring that erupts with jets of water and steam at intervals.

clue.text: Author, one with a flower

parts.note: Roald Dahl, author of Charlie and the Chocolate Factory
the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A writer holding a single bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: The dahlia is a garden plant with large showy blooms, named after the botanist Anders Dahl.

clue.text: Loss of the French? Fate uncertain

parts.note: de is French for of

indicators.note: something uncertain is unsettled, so the letters are not fixed in their order

parts.note: letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Wondering whether the French side will lose, its destiny still in the balance.
explanation.definitionFit: A defeat is a loss in a contest or battle, the opposite of a victory.

clue.text: Accommodated in dilapidated shed, you blow your top

indicators.note: in places one part inside the other
a dilapidated building is falling apart, so its letters are jumbled

parts.note: letters to be rearranged

indicators.note: losing your top means the first letter is lost

parts.note: taken as written before its first letter goes

explanation.surface: Stuck in a tumbledown hut, you lose your temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blow your top' means getting angry, but here it removes the top letter of 'you'.
explanation.definitionFit: To house someone is to give them a place to live, so housed means accommodated.

clue.text: You hear animal

indicators.note: what you hear is a sound, so the spoken form counts

parts.note: the pronoun, said out loud

explanation.surface: Telling someone they can hear a creature nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: A ewe is a female sheep, an example of an animal.

clue.text: Some of the wives trying to find a place to dress

indicators.note: some of means only part, so the letters sit inside the words that follow

parts.note: spanning the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: Several wives are hunting for a changing room.
explanation.definitionFit: A vestry is the church room where clergy and choir put on their robes.

clue.text: Quarter of Scottish river, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is the spoken word, not its spelling

parts.note: the Forth is the river flowing through Stirling into the Firth of Forth

explanation.surface: A section of a river in Scotland, so people say.
explanation.definitionFit: A fourth is one of four equal parts, which is what a quarter is.

clue.text: Cuts material taxes

parts.note: lace is a delicate fabric
rates are local property taxes in Britain

explanation.surface: Tax cuts on cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: To lacerate is to tear or gash flesh, so lacerates means cuts deeply.
